_comment: Doctrine and faction classification for every base aircraft, used when the runtime
aircraft data carries no recognisable ai block.
The published warfare_wings 1.1.4 jar ships 90 aircraft JSON files and NONE of them
contains an 'ai' object: AircraftMetadataResolver therefore falls through to
string(ai, 'doctrine', 'unknown') and every aircraft outside the hand-authored fighter
fixture is born doctrine='unknown'. Role already survives that gap because resolve()
backfills it from BenchmarkCategory; doctrine had no equivalent path until this file.
This table is not invented. It is the mod author's own ai block, read from
data/warfare_wings/aircraft/*.json in this repository, where it has been present since
the initial import. Two corrections were applied on top of it, recorded below.

_provenance.runtime_gap: warfare_wings-1.1.4-1.20.1-forge.jar: 90 aircraft JSON entries, 0 with an ai block
corrections: The authored data marks all six heavy aircraft 'escort'. Escort is a mission type, not a
combat doctrine for the aircraft being escorted, and it collapses two distinct behaviours
into one label. B-17, B-29, G10N1, G10N2 and He 111 are reclassified 'level_bomber';
G4M, whose authored role is already torpedo_bomber, is reclassified 'torpedo_attack'.
The 14 fighters and 4 attackers are used exactly as authored.

_contract: Every base aircraft id below must resolve to a doctrine that AutopilotDoctrine recognises.
AircraftClassificationGameTests enforces that, and also pins the 3 turn_fighter / 11
energy_fighter split so a future edit cannot silently downgrade the qualified fighters.
